summary:
ASTRA is a program that allows astronauts to monitor their health during space missions using AI technology. The program includes health monitoring, AI voice assistance, and body mapping. Astronauts can point to certain parts of their body by camera or ask ASTRA questions by voice command. Health information used in the program includes such data as results of blood tests, urine tests, and vital signs.

Autonomous Spaceflight Health Assessment and Response Assistant (ASTRA) is a preventive system that does not wait until the symptoms appear. The program presents health trends using graphs, and gives advice concerning exercises, nutrition, and monitoring. Moreover, the program tells how space radiation, microgravity, and isolation influence the human body.

The significance of the project is connected with the fact that astronauts have specific health problems that cannot be monitored so far from Earth. ASTRA simplifies health information for astronauts and allows them to solve some health problems before they become serious.
details:
What It Does/How It Works:

ASTRA is an astronaut health monitoring tool that helps promote physical and mental health. ASTRA uses NASA’s 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight framework incorporating research from NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP), Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) and Canadian Space Agency (CSA).

ASTRA monitors important health metrics like calcium levels in urine, heart rate, sleep, blood oxygen levels, red blood cells, white blood cells, muscle strength and bone density. The astronaut can record their health metrics, document any symptoms they may be experiencing and use the webcam to highlight areas of their body using an interactive anatomy avatar.

Once data has been recorded, ASTRA will analyse this to see if there are any concerning trends. The AI virtual assistant gives the astronaut an evidence-based and tailored explanation of their health and recommendations. Other features include voice recording, English and French language support, prompts and health summaries in case of emergencies.

Benefits:

ASTRA helps astronauts understand complex physiological data. Using the interactive dashboard, astronauts can learn how their physical and mental health is changing. This is done through visualising trends, recording data and having a tailored AI assistant.

This is very important in deep space missions due to delays in communication. ASTRA provides early awareness, evidence-based decisions and a means to communicate any issues to medical staff. ASTRA provides monitoring and decision-making tools but does not diagnose.

Impact on Space and Earth:

Space: ASTRA helps astronauts stay healthy on long term missions such as Artemis and Mars. The astronauts can track any changes in their physiology which could be caused by microgravity, radiation, isolation etc. A bone mineral density loss of around 1%-1.5% per month can occur in certain load bearing bones when in microgravity so monitoring bone health is very important.

Earth: The technology used in ASTRA could help with telehealth. With its easy to use design and low bandwidth requirements it could be used in rural clinics, isolated work environments and communities needing continuous health monitoring. For example those at risk of osteoporosis.

Tools/Languages/Hardware/Software:

TypeScript, React, JavaScript, HTML and CSS were used to create ASTRA. Version control was kept using GitHub.

The technologies used include:

  • AI – Voice assistant, voice recognition, tailored answers and bilingual options.
  • Computer Vision – MediaPipe pose detection and hand detection using webcam.
  • Data Visualisation – Interactive dashboards and charts.
  • Health Data – Tracking health, tracking what day of mission and having tailored data.
  • Anatomy – Interactive avatar linking health to different parts of the body.
  • Emergency Support – Summarising health data.

Research was carried out using research from NASA’s HRP, the relevant datasets from OSDR and resources from CSA. Public domain images were also used from NASA’s Image and Video Library. The 30 second demo video was made using Canva and Scratch.

Creativity/Innovation:

ASTRA includes interactive technologies such as AI, webcam to highlight areas of the body, anatomy and monitoring long-term physiological changes.

Key innovations include:

  • Voice AI Assistant – Astronaut can ask health related questions.
  • Interactive Anatomy Avatar – Links health data and educational data to specific areas of the body.
  • Tailored Trend Analysis – Identifies any concerning changes in recorded health data.
  • Emergency Support – Summarises health data.
  • Bilingual – English and French.

Evidence-Based Recommendations – Gives tailored explanations and recommendations based on the recorded data and relevant evidence.

All of these features help to simplify complex health data and encourage astronauts to get involved with their health.

Key considerations:

  • Constraints in Space – ASTRA has been designed with limitations of spacecraft in mind. This includes lightweight testing methods, wearable devices and using existing cameras in the cabin.
  • Scientifically Accurate/Medical Safety – ASTRA knows the difference between recorded data, potential trends and actual medical conditions. ASTRA provides decision-making tools.
  • Reliable Data/Tailored – Answers given from AI are based on the health data available and relevant evidence. Missing information has also been considered.
  • Gravity – ASTRA considers the differences in physiology between microgravity, lunar gravity (~1/6g) and Martian gravity (~3/8g). Especially relating to bone health.
  • Easy to Understand/Communicate – Voice recognition, bilingual, visual trends and health summaries makes health data easier to understand.
